tracker.reason: Its terms pages need a browser to read and have not been read yet, and its server takes only a browser sign-in.

No clause against publishing was found in PayPal's Developer Testing Agreement or User Agreement on 2026-10-17, but no terms specific to its MCP server were found either. Its tokens last only hours, so it waits for a tracker job that renews a browser sign-in.

The Atlassian Customer Agreement (section 2.4) forbids publishing assessments of free or beta products, and a tracker account would be free. Paid products may be assessed in public only with everything needed to repeat the assessment.

Cloudflare's terms allow publishing benchmarks with everything needed to repeat them (section 2.2.2), but treat anything learned about a beta service as confidential (section 5). Whether this server is beta has not been checked, and it takes only a browser sign-in.
Sentry's terms (section 2.3(g)) forbid publishing benchmarks or performance information about the service, and treat any technical information about it as confidential.
Intercom's terms forbid publishing performance information about the service.
